docs.title: JST CRM Runbook
docs.text:
How to deploy, look after and fix the CRM. Written for whoever is on duty, including when the usual person is away. You do not need to be an engineer: every page is a short list of steps you can follow one at a time.

Something is broken right now?

Go straight to The site is down: first five minutes.

docs.title: Pick what you need
docs.text: I want to... Go to Open a terminal on the server Connect with SSH Understand how code reaches the server How a deploy happens Deploy when automation is down Deploy by hand Undo a bad release Go back Check the CRM is healthy Daily health check Back up the data Take and copy a backup Change a password or key Passwords and keys Bring data back Restore the database

docs.title: What the CRM is made of
docs.text:
Think of it as five boxes that run together on one server:

Box What it does web The website staff open. It is the part you see in the browser. api The brain. It receives what staff do and talks to the database. db The database. All the files, accounts and money records live here. migrate A helper that updates the database's shape on every deploy, then stops. It is meant to show as "Exited". driver-api A separate service for the drivers' phone app.

All five are run by a tool called Docker Compose. A volume is the folder Docker keeps data in, so the data survives when a box is restarted. The two that matter are the database volume and the backups volume.

docs.title: The golden rules
docs.text:
1. Back up before any risky change. See Backups.
  2. Never delete a Docker volume. Never run docker compose down -v or docker volume prune on the server. That erases the database.
  3. Read the error before you act. Most problems are solved by the site-down page.
  4. Write down what you did, with the time, so the next person knows.

docs.title: Who to contact
docs.text:
(Name, phone, role. Fill this in.)

Keep this site free of secrets

GitHub Pages sites are public. Never write passwords, keys, IP addresses or customer data on these pages.

docs.title: Connect to the server (SSH)
docs.text: When to use this: Any page that says "open a terminal on the server". Time it takes: 5 minutes (first time: 15) You need: The server's address and your username, from the person who manages access. A computer on the office network (or the VPN, if you use one).

docs.title: What SSH is
docs.text:
SSH lets you type commands on the server from your own computer, over a secure connection. You do not need to be in the same room as the server.

The address and username are not on this site

This site is public, so the real server address and usernames are kept private. Ask the developer for them, or look in the team's password manager. In the steps below, replace <username> and <server-address>.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] You have your username and the server address (a name like crm-server.local or numbers like 192.168.x.x).
  • [ ] You are on the office network or connected to the VPN.
  • [ ] Your computer has a terminal: Mac (open Terminal), Windows 10/11 (open PowerShell), Linux (any terminal). All three already include SSH.

docs.title: Steps: the first time
docs.text:
1. Create your own key (a digital ID card for your computer). Skip if you have done this before. When it asks for a passphrase, choose one and remember it.
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your-name-laptop"

Press Enter to accept the default file location.

  1. Show your public key and copy the whole line it prints (starts with ssh-ed25519).
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

On Windows PowerShell use type $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub.

  1. Send the public key to the person who manages the server. They add it to the server. Send only the .pub file's contents.

!!! danger "Never share the private key" The file without .pub (id_ed25519) stays on your computer. Never send it, paste it in chat, or put it on GitHub.

  1. Connect.
ssh <username>@<server-address>
  1. The first time, it asks:
Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no)?

Type yes and press Enter. This only happens once per server.

  1. Enter your key's passphrase if asked. You are in when the prompt changes to something like username@server:~$.

  2. Go to the CRM folder (the one that contains compose.yml). Ask the developer for its location, then:

cd <crm-folder>
ls

You should see compose.yml in the list.

docs.title: Make it shorter next time
docs.text:
Create or edit the file ~/.ssh/config on your computer and add:

Host crm
    HostName <server-address>
    User <username>

Now you only type:

ssh crm

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
hostname
docker compose version

The first shows the server's name, not your computer's. The second shows a Docker version. Now you can follow any page on this site.

docs.title: Leaving the server
docs.text:
exit

Always exit when you are done. Do not leave a connection open and unattended.

docs.title: Safety rules
docs.text:
• Only use your own key. Never share keys or logins.
  • Do not type a command you do not understand. Ask first.
  • Never run docker compose down -v or docker volume prune: they erase the database.
  • If your laptop is lost or stolen, tell the person managing the server at once so they remove your key.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this Connection timed out You are not on the office network or VPN, or the server is off. Check your network, then see The server is gone. Connection refused The server is on, but SSH is not running or the address is wrong. Ask the developer. Permission denied (publickey) Your key was not added yet, or you used the wrong username. Send your public key again and check the username. Host key verification failed or a big warning about REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED The server was rebuilt or something is wrong. Stop and ask the developer. Do not just delete the warning. Could not resolve hostname Typo in the address, or you are off the network. Too many authentication failures Use ssh -o IdentitiesOnly=yes <username>@<server-address>.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: A database update failed
docs.text: When to use this: A deploy stopped, and the migrate box did not finish with Exited (0). Time it takes: 20 minutes You need: A terminal on the server, and a backup from before the deploy.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text: Every deploy first runs migrate, a helper that changes the database's shape to match the new code (for example, adding a column). If it fails, the CRM refuses to start on purpose. That protects the data: a new program on an old database would give errors on every page.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Do not try to repair the database by hand.
  • [ ] Find the backup taken before the deploy (Backups).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Read why it failed:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml logs migrate

  1. Copy the last 20 lines and send them to the developer. They will fix the update in the code.

  2. To get staff working again now, go back to the last good version: Go back.

  3. If the failed update partly changed the database (the log shows some steps succeeded before the error), the old program may not run on it. Restore the backup taken before the deploy, then go back.

  4. When the developer has fixed it, push the fix. The normal deploy runs the update again.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• migrate shows Exited (0).
  • The CRM opens and you can sign in.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this could not connect to server in the migrate log The database was not ready or is down: The site is down The same failure after going back Restore the pre-deploy backup

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Restore the database from a backup
docs.text:
When to use this: Data was lost or damaged, a bad update broke the database, or you are rebuilding a server. Time it takes: 20 minutes You need: A terminal on the server and a backup file (.dump). See Backups.

This replaces everything in the live database

Anything entered after the backup was taken is lost. Tell staff to stop using the CRM first. If the database still starts, take a fresh backup of it before you begin, in case you restore the wrong file.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Staff told to stop working in the CRM.
  • [ ] You know which backup file you are restoring and when it was taken.
  • [ ] The file is on the server. If it is inside the CRM's backups folder, copy it out:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml cp api:/app/var/backups/<backup-name> ./restore.dump

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to the CRM folder (the one with compose.yml). Set the settings if needed (see The site is down, "Set up your terminal").

  2. Stop everything that uses the database:

docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml stop api driver-api web
  1. Empty the database:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml exec -T db psql -U jst -d postgres -c "DROP DATABASE jst_crm_staging;" -c "CREATE DATABASE jst_crm_staging;"
  1. Load the backup:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml exec -T db pg_restore -U jst -d jst_crm_staging --no-owner < restore.dump

A few warning lines are usually harmless. A line starting with error that stops the command is not.

  1. Start everything again:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml up -d

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml ps shows all boxes running.
  • Sign in and open a recent file. Check its details look right.
  • Open a report, such as the trial balance, and check the totals look reasonable.
  • Tell staff which date and time the data goes back to, so they can re-enter anything missing.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this database ... is being accessed by other users at step 3 Step 2 did not stop everything. Run step 2 again and check with ps. pg_restore: error: input file does not appear to be a valid archive Wrong file, or it was damaged while copying. Try another backup. psql: not found or service "db" is not running Start only the database: docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml up -d db, wait a minute, retry. The api starts but shows errors about missing columns The backup is from before a database update. Run docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml run --rm migrate then restart.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: The server is gone
docs.text:
When to use this: The machine died, was stolen, cannot be reached, or its disk is destroyed. Time it takes: About an hour, plus waiting for downloads You need: GitHub admin access, a new Linux machine, and the latest backup copy that is stored off the server.

This is why backups must be copied off the server

If the only backups were on the dead machine, the data may be gone. Check first: a laptop, a cloud drive, a colleague's computer.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Find the newest .dump backup file. Note its date.
  • [ ] Tell staff the CRM is down and roughly when it will be back.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Prepare a new machine. Install Linux, then Docker and Docker Compose. Make sure it has a fixed address on the office network.

  2. Get the code. Follow step 1 of Deploy by hand.

  3. Connect it to GitHub's automatic deploy (optional but best): on GitHub → the repo → Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner, follow the instructions, and give it the same labels as the old one (ask the developer for them).

  4. Start the CRM on an empty database: follow steps 2 to 4 of Deploy by hand.

  5. Load the data: follow Restore the database with your newest backup.

  6. Restore the drivers' connection. The drivers' phones reach the CRM through a secure tunnel run by Cloudflare. The new machine needs the tunnel program installed and signed in. Ask the developer; it needs the Cloudflare account.

  7. Tell staff the new address if it changed.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• You can sign in, open a recent file and run a report.
  • A driver can sign in on their phone.
  • A new backup has been taken and copied off the machine.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text: You see Do this No backup can be found Check every device and cloud account the team uses. Contact the developer immediately. The newest backup is old Restore it anyway, then ask staff to re-enter work done since that date.

docs.title: Afterwards
docs.text:
Write down how it happened, and fix the gap: automatic nightly backups that are copied off the machine.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: The site is down: first five minutes
docs.text:
When to use this: Staff cannot open the CRM, pages do not load, or everything shows errors. Time it takes: 5 minutes to find the cause You need: A terminal on the server (how to connect).

Stay calm, change one thing at a time

The data is safe in the database volume. Most problems are fixed by restarting. Do not delete anything.

docs.title: Set up your terminal
docs.text:
1. Go to the CRM folder (the one with compose.yml).
  2. Docker needs to know which version is running. Find it:
docker ps --format '{{.Image}}' | grep ghcr

Then use it (replace with what you saw):

export CRM_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tareqjdtours/jst-crm-backend:<code>

If nothing is listed because everything is stopped, use the code of the last green deploy in GitHub's Actions tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Is anything running?
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml ps

Look for db, api, web. Any box that is Exited, restarting or unhealthy is the suspect. (migrate showing Exited (0) is fine.)

  1. Is the computer itself OK?
df -h

A disk at 100% stops the database. Tell the developer; do not delete Docker volumes.

  1. Read the last messages.
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml logs --tail=100 api db migrate

  1. Match what you see with the table below.

  2. If unsure, do a clean restart. It keeps all data.

docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml down
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml up -d

Never add -v to down: it erases the database.

docs.title: What you see and what to do
docs.text: You see Meaning Do this Pages load but every action says 502 The website lost track of the api Clean restart (step 5) api never starts; migrate is not Exited (0) A database update failed A database update failed Errors about a missing column or table New code, old database shape docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml run --rm migrate, then restart db is not running Database stopped Check the disk (step 2), then up -d. If it will not start: Restore the database "Too many attempts" (429) when signing in Sign-in throttle Wait a few minutes Staff sign in but are signed out at once The address is plain http and the cookie needs https Ask the developer Drivers cannot sign in, office is fine The driver service or its tunnel Check curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/driver/health; ask the developer to check the tunnel The whole server does not respond Machine is off or the network is down The server is gone A deploy just failed New version did not start Go back

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
curl -fsS http://localhost:5180/api/v1/health/ready

You should see "status":"ok". Then sign in from a browser and open a recent file.

docs.title: After it is fixed
docs.text:
• Write down what happened, what you did, and the times.
  • Tell the team the site is back.
  • Take a fresh backup.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: How a deploy happens (CI/CD)
docs.text: When to use this: You want to know what happens when code is pushed, or why a deploy turned red. Time it takes: 5 minutes to read

docs.title: The idea in one line
docs.text: When a developer pushes code to the main branch on GitHub, robots test it, package it and put it on the server. Nobody has to log in to the server. CI/CD is just the name for this: continuous integration (test it) and continuous delivery (ship it).

docs.title: The three stages
docs.text:
Open the repo's Actions tab on GitHub to watch them. Each stage must pass before the next one starts.

  1. Test. A temporary database is created and the automatic tests run. If a test fails, nothing is shipped. The live site is not touched.
  2. Build. The code is packaged into an image (a sealed copy of the program) and stored on GitHub, labelled with the commit's unique code.
  3. Deploy. The deploy machine downloads that image, stops the old CRM, starts the new one, and then asks the CRM "are you healthy?" every 10 seconds for up to two minutes.

The site is briefly down during stage 3

The old version is stopped before the new one starts, usually for a minute or two. Deploy outside office hours when you can. Data is kept: the database volume is never removed.

docs.title: The front end is shipped with the backend
docs.text:
The website's screens (the front end) live in a separate repository, but they are built during the backend's deploy. So:

Tip

Pushing a front-end change on its own does not update the live site. Re-run the backend workflow: GitHub → Actions → Backend CI → open the latest run → Re-run all jobs.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• All three stages show a green tick in the Actions tab.
  • The last step says "Staging is healthy!".
  • Open the CRM in a browser and sign in.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this Red at Test A code problem. Tell the developer. The live site is unaffected. Red at Build A packaging problem. Re-run the job once; if it fails again, tell the developer. Red at Deploy, "Staging failed health verification" The new version did not start. The old one is already stopped, so the site is down. Follow The site is down, then Go back. Stuck on "Waiting for a runner" The deploy machine is off or offline. Use Deploy by hand.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Deploy by hand
docs.text:
When to use this: The automatic deploy is down, or you are setting up a new server. Time it takes: 20 minutes You need: A terminal on the server, Docker installed, the GitHub repo access, and the three CRM secrets (database password, signing key, first-admin password) from whoever holds them.

Normally you do not do this

Pushing to main deploys automatically. See How a deploy happens.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Take a backup if the CRM is already running.
  • [ ] Decide which version to deploy. Each version is labelled with a commit code, visible in the GitHub Actions tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Get the code. Skip if it is already on the server.
git clone git@github.com:tareqjdtours/jst-crm-backend.git
cd jst-crm-backend
git clone git@github.com:tareqjdtours/jst-crm-frontend.git

The front end must sit inside the backend folder, named jst-crm-frontend.

  1. Give the terminal its settings. Replace each ... with the real value. Never save these in a file in the repo.
export POSTGRES_PASSWORD=...
export JWT_SECRET=...
export SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD=...
export JOFOTARA_MODE=off
export CRM_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tareqjdtours/jst-crm-backend:<commit-code>

These last only until you close the terminal.

  1. Log in to GitHub's image store and download the version. Use a GitHub token that can read packages.
echo <github-token> | docker login ghcr.io -u <github-username> --password-stdin
docker pull "$CRM_IMAGE"
  1. Start everything. Always include both -f files.
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml up -d --build
  • -d runs it in the background.

  • --build rebuilds the website part.

  • New server only: create the first admin and the starting lists.

docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml exec api uv run --no-sync python scripts/seed_reference.py --admin-email you@example.com

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml ps
  • Every box says running or healthy.
  • migrate says Exited (0). That is correct; it is a one-time job.
curl -fsS http://localhost:5180/api/v1/health/ready

You should see "status":"ok". Then open http://<server>:5180 and sign in.

docs.title: Building the image yourself
docs.text:
Only if GitHub's image store is unavailable. In the backend folder:

docker build -t crm-local:manual .
export CRM_IMAGE=crm-local:manual

Then do step 4. If your computer and the server have different processor types (for example a Mac with an M-chip and a normal Linux server), build on the server itself, or add --platform linux/amd64. Tag with the commit code so you can tell later what is running.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this invalid reference format or a warning about unset variables Step 2 was skipped. Set the variables again in this terminal. denied when pulling The GitHub token is wrong or cannot read packages. Site loads but every action gives 502 Run docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml down then step 4 again. migrate is not Exited (0) See A database update failed.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Go back to the last working version
docs.text: When to use this: A new version broke something and you need the old one back. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: A terminal on the server; the commit code of the last good version.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Take a backup of the current database.
  • [ ] Find the last good version's commit code: GitHub → Actions → pick the last run that worked → copy the code after the colon in the image name, or the commit code on that run.

Going back does not undo database changes

Each deploy may change the database's shape. Going back runs the old program on the new database shape. This usually works, but if the change removed something the old program needs, you must also restore the database from the backup taken before the bad deploy.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open a terminal on the server and go to the CRM folder (the one with compose.yml).

  2. Set the old version and the settings (see Deploy by hand, step 2):

export CRM_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tareqjdtours/jst-crm-backend:<old-commit-code>
  1. Download it:
docker pull "$CRM_IMAGE"
  1. Restart on the old version:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml down
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml up -d --build

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml ps shows all boxes running.
  • Open the CRM and sign in; open a recent file.

The next push redeploys the new code

The server now runs the old version, but GitHub's main still holds the bad code. Ask the developer to fix or revert it before the next push, or the bad version comes back.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this Errors mention a missing column or table The database is ahead of the code. Restore the database. Cannot pull the old image It may have been deleted. Build it from the old commit: see "Building the image yourself" in Deploy by hand.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Take and copy a backup
docs.text: When to use this: Every day, and always before a risky change (a deploy, a go-back, a restore). Time it takes: 5 minutes You need: A CRM login with the backup permission, or a terminal on the server.

docs.title: Why two steps
docs.text: A backup is a single file with a copy of the whole database. But if it stays on the same server as the database, a broken server takes both. Always keep at least one copy somewhere else (another computer, a cloud drive).

docs.title: Steps: from the CRM
docs.text:
1. Sign in and open System Control → Database Backup.
  2. Type a name (letters, numbers, dash and underscore only, for example before-update-2026-11-01) and click Take backup.
  3. When it appears in the list, download it and save it somewhere safe off the server.

docs.title: Steps: from the server
docs.text:
1. Go to the CRM folder (the one with compose.yml).
  2. Make a dated backup file:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml exec -T db pg_dump -U jst -Fc jst_crm_staging > jst_crm-$(date +%F).dump
  1. Copy the file off the server (for example with scp, or a cloud drive).

docs.title: Copy the backups taken from the CRM screen
docs.text: docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml cp api:/app/var/backups ./backups-copy

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• The file exists and is not tiny (a few kilobytes means it failed).
  • Check its size: ls -lh jst_crm-*.dump.
  • A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a backup. Once, on a spare machine, follow Restore the database.

Uploaded documents

Contracts and scans uploaded to the CRM are stored as files, separate from the database. A database backup does not contain them. Ask the developer to confirm where they are kept on the server and include that folder in your copies.

docs.title: Make it automatic (optional)
docs.text: Ask the developer to schedule the server command above every night, and to delete copies older than about 30 days.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this "backup_unavailable" or "backup_failed" in the CRM The disk may be full (df -h). Use the server command instead. "backup already exists" Pick a different name. service "db" is not running The database is stopped: The site is down.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Daily health check
docs.text: When to use this: Every morning, or any time you want to be sure the CRM is OK. Time it takes: 2 minutes You need: A browser. A terminal on the server for the full check.

docs.title: Quick check (no terminal)
docs.text:
1. Open the CRM and sign in.
  2. Open a recent file. It should load with its details.
  3. Open the health address in the browser: http://<server>:5180/api/v1/health/ready

You should see {"status":"ok","db":"ok", ...}. "db":"down" means the website is up but the database is not.

docs.title: Full check (on the server)
docs.text:
1. Go to the CRM folder (the one with compose.yml).

  2. See every box:

docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml ps

Good looks like: db, api, web, driver-api are running or healthy; migrate is Exited (0).

  1. Look at the latest messages from the api:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml logs --tail=50 api

A few lines are normal. A long run of the word ERROR is not.

  1. Check there is disk space left. A full disk stops the database.
df -h

Worry when the main disk is above about 85% used.

  1. Check a recent backup exists. See Backups.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this A box is restarting or unhealthy The site is down db: down The site is down, step 4 Disk above 85% Tell the developer. Do not delete Docker volumes.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Change a password or key
docs.text: When to use this: A password was shared by mistake, someone left the team, or a staff member is locked out. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: GitHub admin access to the CRM repository (for keys) or a terminal on the server (for a user's password).

docs.title: A staff member is locked out or forgot their password
docs.text:
There is no email reset link. An administrator sets a new one from the server.

  1. Go to the CRM folder (the one with compose.yml).
  2. Run this, replacing the email:
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.staging.yml run --rm migrate uv run --no-sync python scripts/reset_password.py someone@example.com
  1. Type the new password when asked. It will not show on screen. Minimum 8 characters.
  2. Tell the person the temporary password in person or by phone, never by email. The command also signs them out everywhere.

docs.title: Sign everyone out (a key was leaked)
docs.text:
The sign-in key (JWT_SECRET) proves that a sign-in is genuine. Changing it logs everyone out, including drivers.

  1. On GitHub: the CRM backend repo → Settings → Environments → staging → edit the secret JWT_SECRET and paste a new long random value.
  2. Re-run the deploy: Actions → Backend CI → latest run → Re-run all jobs.

Note

The staff service and the driver service must use the same key. The deploy sets both from the same secret, so this happens automatically.

docs.title: Other secrets
docs.text: Secret Where it lives What changing it does POSTGRES_PASSWORD GitHub environment secret Needs the database's own password changed too. Ask the developer; do not change it alone. SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD GitHub environment secret Only used when creating the very first admin. E-invoicing keys GitHub environment settings Ask the developer.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• The person can sign in with the new password.
  • After a key change, you are asked to sign in again.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this "Password too short" Use 8 or more characters. "No such user" Check the email spelling.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD
